Fragmentation and shoreline retreat become unmistakable.
Large exposed surfaces change moisture and thermal behavior across the basin.

Road corridors and clearings increase fragmentation along the frontier arc.
Disturbance mosaics become easier to trace in optical and SWIR-focused views.

viewModes.note: Assign any band to red, green, or blue

natural.title: Visible context
natural.copy: Natural-color style interpretation is strongest for orientation, land-water context, clouds, and communicating broad landscape patterns to non-specialists.
natural.indexContext: This mode is not a computed spectral index. It is your baseline visual interpretation mode for place context and change storytelling.

vegetation.title: Vegetation signal
vegetation.copy: Healthy vegetation typically absorbs red light and reflects strongly in the near infrared. That red-versus-NIR contrast is why NDVI works so well for crop vigor and ecosystem greenness.
vegetation.indexContext: Higher NDVI usually means denser or healthier green vegetation. Values dropping through time can signal clearing, stress, drought, or urban expansion.

water.title: Water and moisture signal
water.copy: Water is usually dark in NIR and SWIR relative to surrounding land, while green reflectance can remain comparatively stronger. That helps highlight open water and moisture patterns.
water.indexContext: Higher NDWI generally points toward stronger water or wetness signals, while falling values can indicate drying, shoreline retreat, or vegetation loss of moisture.

burn.title: Burn severity and disturbance signal
burn.copy: Recently burned surfaces usually lose the strong NIR response of healthy vegetation and become more distinct in SWIR, which is why NBR is widely used for wildfire assessment.
burn.indexContext: Lower or negative NBR values often indicate recent burn or severe disturbance, while recovery through time tends to push the index back upward.

urban.title: Built-up surface signal
urban.copy: Urban materials and exposed soils often become more distinct in SWIR-oriented interpretation. NDBI helps emphasize built-up intensity relative to vegetation-rich surfaces.
urban.indexContext: Higher NDBI often points toward stronger built-up signatures, especially where vegetation is sparse and impervious surfaces dominate.

thermal.title: Surface temperature signal
thermal.copy: Thermal measurements show emitted energy rather than reflected visible light. They are especially valuable for urban heat, evapotranspiration, drought, and water-use interpretation.
thermal.indexContext: Higher LST can indicate hotter built-up areas, dry soils, stressed vegetation, or post-disturbance surfaces depending on the landscape context.

custom.title: Custom composite
custom.copy: Every fixed preset above is really just a choice of which three bands become red, green, and blue. Make that choice yourself and see how it changes what stands out.
custom.indexContext: There is no single computed index here. Choose the band assignment that best isolates the feature you are studying, then compare the result against the fixed presets.
